enrichment_basis.note: Anthropology has NO standalone CCMAS programme (confirmed). Enriched from (a) CCMAS Sociology (SOC) for the shared social-science core, and (b) the Nigerian academic curriculum standard below for the anthropology-specific body of knowledge.

sources.institution: University of Nigeria, Nsukka (UNN) — Dept. of Sociology & Anthropology
sources.role: primary — dedicated ANT course list with units

sources.institution: Nnamdi Azikiwe University (UNIZIK) — Dept. of Sociology & Anthropology

courses.title: Introduction to Anthropology
courses.content: Anthropological perspective; human origins/evolution; dating methods; origins of agriculture and cities; language and culture; concept of culture; socialization; kinship; uses of anthropology.

courses.title: Language in Society and Culture
courses.content: Social/cultural functions of language with reference to Nigeria and West Africa; language and social development; language problems of new states; language policy.

courses.title: History of Sociological and Anthropological Thought
courses.content: Early Western contributions to modern sociology; pioneers of social anthropology (England), cultural anthropology (America), ethnography (France); convergence and divergence.

courses.title: African Social Institutions
courses.content: Ethnographic description/analysis of African societies, peoples, cultures; cultural regions; social organization, institutions, polity, world views; impact of change and modernization.

courses.title: Symbolic Anthropology
courses.content: Key concepts via Durkheim, Evans-Pritchard, Levi-Strauss, Leach, Douglas; mythical thought, ritual, oral traditions as collective representation; relevance to African historiography.

courses.title: Nigerian Peoples and Cultures
courses.content: Survey of Nigeria's peoples/cultures: geographic distribution, linguistic classification, religion, world views, habitat, economy, kinship, marriage, descent, polities; continuity, conflict and change.

courses.title: Anthropology of Peasant Societies
courses.content: Historical evolution and definition of peasantry; social institutions, modes of production, property relations, social formations, types of peasant societies, social transformations.

courses.title: African Religious Systems
courses.content: Theories/concepts of African beliefs/practices; religious foundations of morality; symbols, rituals, worship; case studies; African religion in social change.

courses.title: Political Anthropology
courses.content: Social conditions affecting African government/politics; pressure groups across pre-colonial/colonial/post-colonial periods; colonialism, nationalism, imperialism, neo-colonialism, socialism, liberation movements.

courses.title: Traditional Legal Systems
courses.content: Concepts/nature of 'primitive' law; overlap between law, religion, political control; flexibility of applied law; law and morality; continuity and change in traditional law.

courses.title: Contemporary African Social Thought
courses.content: Social/political ideas of African thinkers (colonial and post-independence); pan-Africanism, ethnic nationalism, Ujaama, humanism, consciencism, revolution, traditional conservatism.

courses.title: Comparative African Social Institutions
courses.content: Advanced study of sub-Saharan Africa as ethnological region; African origins of early man; archaeological records; cultural regions; race and racism; language and population migration.

courses.title: Culture and Communication
courses.content: Interrelationships between culture and communication; defining culture and mass communication; media in culture change; Western information imperialism and acculturation in Africa.

courses.title: Race and Ethnic Relations
courses.content: Theories of race and their use to sustain power (Nazism, anti-semitism, colonial domination); growth of ethnic ideology in Africa and its use in acquiring political power.

courses.title: Urban Sociology and Anthropology
courses.content: Urbanization/urbanism phases; linear theory and critique; pre-industrial African cities; race, ethnicity, class in urban centres; rural migration theories; urban Nigeria, problems and prospects.

courses.title: Introduction to Anthropology
courses.content: Basic concepts, theories and methods in anthropological studies; foundation for advanced study.

courses.title: Nigerian Heritage/Cultural Heritage
courses.content: Ethnic groups in Nigeria from traditional settings; culture, religion, occupation, marriage systems, behavioural differences among ethnic groups.

courses.title: Introduction to African Societies and Cultures
courses.content: Different societies of the African continent; their culture, economy, politics, structure and unique characteristics.

courses.title: Language and Culture in Society
courses.content: Language families and the culture of the societies that speak them; inter-disciplinary survey with linguistics.

courses.title: African Social Thought
courses.content: Legacies of African philosophies and political thinkers; communalism, Negritude, Pan-Africanism, Africans in Diaspora.

courses.title: Regional Ethnography of Sub-Saharan Africa
courses.content: Descriptive/interpretative survey of the historical, political, social, cultural, economic factors shaping Africa south of the Sahara.
